item.title: Tinubu departs Abuja for Makkah to pray for Nigeria
item.description: President Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja on Thursday for Makkah, Saudi Arabia, to perform Umrah, an Islamic pilgrimage involving prayers and other religious rites. According to a statement issued on Wednesday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the visit will provide the President an opportunity for spiritual reflection and prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress. While in Makkah, Tinubu is expected to perform the religious rites associated with Umrah and seek Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. Before departing Abuja, the President will commission equipment acquired by the Nigerian Air Force at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport. Tinubu is expected to return to Nigeria next week after completing the spiritual exercise. The statement was dated October 28, 2026. item.title: Djokovic wins Basel opener to boost ATP Finals bid
item.description: Novak Djokovic dug deep to overcome Ugo Humbert in three sets in his opening match in Basel on Wednesday, keeping his bid to qualify for the season-ending ATP Finals on course. The 39-year-old Djokovic dropped the first set but recovered to beat the French left-hander 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 on his first appearance in Basel since 2011. Djokovic strengthened his chances of a record 19th qualification for the ATP Finals by winning the China Open in Beijing earlier this month, the 102nd title of his career. That was followed by an early exit at the Shanghai Masters, with the 24-time Grand Slam champion accepting a wild card into the Swiss event after slipping to 11th in the Race to Turin standings. Djokovic is a seven-time winner of the ATP Finals, but he did not compete at either of the past two editions because of injury. Only the top eight players qualify for the November 15-22 showpiece, although Jannik Sinner has already pulled out due to a knee problem. Fourth seed Djokovic takes on Germany’s Jan-Lennard Struff in the next round in Basel. He holds an 8-0 record against Struff. item.title: 2027 budget to be ready before end of December – FG
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE MINISTER of State for Budget, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite, on Wednesday assured that the 2027 budget will be ready for presentation before the end of 2026 to allow for legislative consideration ahead of the new fiscal year. The Minister disclosed while fielding questions from State House correspondents at the end of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja. “We are working on the 2027 budget, and our intention is to present it before the end of the year,” Uzoka-Anite said. The planned timeline is expected to give the National Assembly an opportunity to scrutinise the proposed estimates and deliberate on the government’s revenue projections and expenditure priorities before the commencement of the 2027 fiscal year. The annual budget serves as the Federal Government’s principal fiscal policy instrument, setting out its spending priorities, revenue expectations and economic objectives for the year. The minister also announced that the council approved the revised 2026 national policy on food and nutrition in Nigeria and the National Nutrition Bill 2026. She said the documents were developed through collaboration among the office of the vice-president, the ministries of budget and economic planning, agriculture, livestock, education and health, as well as the private sector, the national assembly, and development partners. According to the minister, the documents provide a framework for coordinating and implementing food and nutrition programmes nationwide, while promoting sustainable funding and accountability. She said the measures are aimed at improving the health and wellbeing of Nigerians by reducing childhood stunting, adding that the nutrition bill, an executive bill, would be forwarded to the national assembly for consideration. item.title: 2027: PDP dismisses alleged election postponement plot
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has dismissed allegations of a plot to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to postpone the January 16, 2027 presidential election, insisting that the polls will hold peacefully. The party said it was unaware of any move to alter the election timetable, warning that reports circulating on social media could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and threaten national stability. PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, stated this in his response to Vanguard’s inquiry on Wednesday, expressing confidence that President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and INEC would adhere to the established electoral timetable. “We have seen some of the stories circulating on social media, but I do not believe them, and the PDP does not believe there is any plan whatsoever to alter the election timetable,” Jungudo said. He said the APC-led government and INEC were committed to conducting the elections in accordance with the Electoral Act and the commission’s published schedule of activities. Jungudo alleged that those spreading the reports were attempting to create confusion because they had realised they would make little impact in the elections. “Some people have clearly realised that they will not make any impact in the elections. What they have decided to do, therefore, is create confusion and undermine confidence in the process by sowing doubts in the minds of Nigerians,” he said. Warning that the consequences could extend beyond partisan politics, Jungudo said any threat to the credibility of the electoral process could affect the country as a whole. “Unfortunately, what they fail to understand is that this will not affect the APC or President Tinubu alone. It will affect Nigeria as a country,” he warned. He urged politicians to moderate their public statements and promote peace, confidence in the electoral process and trust in INEC’s impartiality. Jungudo also challenged opposition parties seeking to defeat the APC to unite and build a formidable political force. “I can assure you that the 2027 elections will hold, and they will hold peacefully, without any crisis, by the special grace of God,” he said. item.title: Niger State Assembly Commends Army For Foiling Attack By Bandits
item.description: ‎ ‎The Niger State House of Assembly has commended troops of the Nigerian Army for repelling a major attack by bandits on communities in Rafi Local Government Area of the state, which left one soldier dead and three others injured. ‎ ‎The House also called for the establishment of additional military bases in vulnerable communities to strengthen security, prevent bandits from regrouping, and improve rapid response to distress calls. ‎ ‎The commendation followed a motion moved by the member representing Rafi Constituency, Zubairu Zanna, during plenary on Tuesday. ‎ ‎The lawmaker praised the troops for their courage, professionalism and gallantry in confronting the armed men, saying their intervention prevented what could have resulted in a massacre of innocent residents. Niger State is in North-Central Nigeria ‎ About two weeks ago, more than 100 suspected bandits reportedly invaded communities along the Zungeru-Tegina Road but were met with stiff resistance from the Army, which successfully repelled the attack. ‎ ‎Although one soldier reportedly died from gunshot injuries while three others sustained injuries, several bandits were neutralised during the encounter, and motorcycles were recovered. ‎ ‎Zanna urged the Nigerian Army and other security agencies to sustain their operations and strengthen their presence in the affected communities to prevent further attacks. ‎ ‎He stressed the strategic and economic importance of the communities, noting that the establishment of a Forward Operating Base (FOB) would help prevent criminal groups from regrouping and launching fresh attacks. ‎ ‎According to him, the absence of military bases and strategically positioned security formations along identified vulnerable corridors could limit the ability of security personnel to respond swiftly to distress calls. ‎ ‎The lawmaker further observed that difficult terrain, extensive forests and inadequately secured rural routes in parts of the state, particularly Rafi Local Government Area, provided opportunities for criminal groups to infiltrate communities, establish camps and hideouts, and launch attacks on innocent residents. ‎ ‎He therefore called on the Niger State Government to urgently engage the Federal Government on the need to establish additional military bases and strengthen security deployments in vulnerable communities, particularly along routes frequently used by bandits. ‎ ‎The Speaker of the House, Abdulmalik Sarkindaji, who presided over the plenary, called for a minute of silence in honour of the fallen soldier and offered prayers for the speedy recovery of those receiving medical treatment. item.title: 92-year-old US judge handling Maduro case dies
item.description: Alvin Hellerstein, the US judge overseeing the case against deposed Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro, has died aged 92, an official confirmed Wednesday. As one of the oldest US federal judges, questions had been raised about whether he was the right justice to preside over what could be a prolonged trial for Maduro on drug trafficking charges. Hellerstein’s lengthy career included overseeing the civil cases arising from Al-Qaeda’s September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on New York and Washington, often rejecting deals he saw as unfair to complainants. His death was confirmed to AFP by an official at the United States District Court, Southern District of New York, where he presided. Hellerstein also tangled with Donald Trump, rejecting a request by the US president to have his New York hush money case moved to federal court. Last year, he blocked the Trump administration from deporting alleged Venezuelan gang members without a court hearing. In a noteworthy 2015 ruling, Hellerstein ordered the US government to release a trove of photos depicting abuse of detainees in Iraq and Afghanistan. He also presided over a trial last year in which a jury found French banking giant BNP Paribas’s work in Sudan had helped prop up the regime of former ruler Omar al-Bashir, awarding $20.75 million in damages to three plaintiffs from Sudan. Hellerstein handled the sprawling drug trafficking case linked to Maduro for over a decade, which has already seen the conviction of Venezuela’s former intelligence chief, Hugo Armando Carvajal. Maduro was seized by US forces in January in a military raid on his compound in Venezuela. A graduate of Columbia University law school, Hellerstein served as a lawyer in the US Army from 1957 to 1960 before entering private practice. He was nominated by then president Bill Clinton in 1998 to be a district court judge for the Southern District of New York. item.title: 2027: Adebayo threatens protest over alleged plot to postpone election
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Adewole Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council has threatened legal action and mass protests against any attempt to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, into postponing the January 16, 2027 presidential election. The council said the election timetable was non-negotiable, warning that any attempt to alter it, including under the guise of public health concerns, would undermine the democratic process and Nigerians’ right to choose their leaders. Speaking to Vanguard in Abuja on Wednesday, the campaign council’s Chief Media and Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, alleged a plot to summon INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, to the Presidential Villa to alter the election timetable. “We strongly condemn any covert or overt attempts to pressure INEC into altering the sacrosanct January 16, 2027, election timetable,” Adebayo said. He accused the Tinubu administration of preparing to manipulate the electoral process, citing what he described as its unpopularity. “We are aware that because of the unprecedented unpopularity of the Tinubu administration and the fact that Nigerians have totally rejected them, they have many rigging cards under their table to play,” he said. Adebayo also warned against using the reported Ebola outbreak as a pretext to delay the election, saying the campaign council would resist any such move through legal means and mass action. “Using public health concerns or engineered crises as political tools to evade an imminent electoral verdict will be fiercely resisted by all legal means, including mass actions,” he said. He urged INEC to remain neutral and reject any alleged pressure from the Presidency, insisting that the election timetable must be maintained. Adebayo said the campaign’s presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and his running mate, Dr Usman Bugaje, remained prepared for the polls, urging Nigerians to remain vigilant. “Nigerians are no fools, and any attempt to treat us that way stands to be stoutly resisted by the mass of Nigerians,” he added. item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Chioma Agwuegbo, executive director of TechHerNG, has called on technology companies to prioritise users’ safety, privacy and rights, warning that the rapid development of digital tools without adequate safeguards could expose women, children and persons with disabilities to greater risks. Agwuegbo spoke during the session titled “Designing Safer Digital Futures: Privacy, Protection and Rights in African Tech” at the Startup Stage of Moonshot 2026: Courage & Conviction. She criticised technology platforms for focusing on developing new products and features without adequately considering their potential harm to users. “Access and safety should be the floor,” she said, arguing that excluding people from safe participation in digital spaces undermines their agency. Agwuegbo cited the misuse of artificial intelligence to create non-consensual intimate images of women as an example of the dangers associated with emerging technologies. “For instance, Grok should never be able to nudify women,” she said, warning that harmful applications can emerge rapidly after new technologies become available. item.title: Pensioners blast NLC, FG over exclusion from ₦70,000 transport relief
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has condemned its exclusion from the newly approved ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers, accusing the Federal Government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) of abandoning retired workers who are battling the same punishing cost of living. NUP National President, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, said the exclusion of pensioners from the six-month intervention — approved for public servants from November 2026 — was “unjust” and a painful reminder that those who spent their productive years in national service are being treated as an afterthought. “Pensioners also depend on public transportation to access hospitals, attend medical appointments, purchase food, and other essential items,” Abumisi said, stressing that many retirees live on inadequate pensions and have no other reliable income. The union questioned why the NLC, which negotiated for serving workers, did not push for corresponding relief for retired colleagues, calling the omission evidence of the “insensitivity of civil servants to the plight of their former colleagues, now retired, whom they will eventually join in retirement.” NUP argued that the welfare of workers and pensioners should not be treated as competing interests, warning that every serving employee will one day become a pensioner. The union also frowned at the government’s failure to pay the ₦25,000 monthly palliative promised under the Federal Government’s October 2, 2023 Memorandum of Understanding with the NLC and TUC. The agreement committed the government to pay ₦25,000 monthly for three months to 15 million households, including vulnerable pensioners — ₦75,000 per eligible beneficiary in total. More than three years later, NUP says many vulnerable pensioners have still not received the money. It demanded that the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, led by Dr. Bernard M. Doro, explain what has stalled the payment and give a definite timeline. The union appealed directly to President Bola Tinubu to intervene urgently and extend the ₦70,000 transport allowance to eligible retirees, or provide an equivalent transport-support measure. NUP warned that it will pursue “all legitimate and lawful avenues” if the government fails to act, insisting that Nigerians who served the country faithfully must not be discarded in retirement. NUP National President, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, said the exclusion of pensioners from the six-month intervention — approved for public servants from November 2026 — was “unjust” and a painful reminder that those who spent their productive years in national service are being treated as an afterthought. “Pensioners also depend on public transportation to access hospitals, attend medical appointments, purchase food, and other essential items,” Abumisi said, stressing that many retirees live on inadequate pensions and have no other reliable income. The union questioned why the NLC, which negotiated for serving workers, did not push for corresponding relief for retired colleagues, calling the omission evidence of the “insensitivity of civil servants to the plight of their former colleagues, now retired, whom they will eventually join in retirement.” NUP argued that the welfare of workers and pensioners should not be treated as competing interests, warning that every serving employee will one day become a pensioner. The union also frowned at the government’s failure to pay the ₦25,000 monthly palliative promised under the Federal Government’s October 2, 2023 Memorandum of Understanding with the NLC and TUC. The agreement committed the government to pay ₦25,000 monthly for three months to 15 million households, including vulnerable pensioners — ₦75,000 per eligible beneficiary in total. More than three years later, NUP says many vulnerable pensioners have still not received the money. It demanded that the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, led by Dr. Bernard M. Doro, explain what has stalled the payment and give a definite timeline. The union appealed directly to President Bola Tinubu to intervene urgently and extend the ₦70,000 transport allowance to eligible retirees, or provide an equivalent transport-support measure. NUP warned that it will pursue “all legitimate and lawful avenues” if the government fails to act, insisting that Nigerians who served the country faithfully must not be discarded in retirement. While such recognition is not a substitute for legal verification, it reflects the company’s publicly stated commitment to protecting property investors and promoting responsible real estate development. MEZIE: QUESTIONS ABOUT CREDIBILITY AND RESPONSIBLE ADVOCACY Chimezie Princewill Onwuka, popularly known as Mezie, has made allegations concerning Odibola Properties and its involvement in disputed land at Mbodo-Aluu, Rivers State. However, an important question deserves public attention: How thoroughly were the relevant legal documents examined before these allegations were presented to the public? There is also a reported disciplinary matter in his past that raises legitimate questions about accountability. If independently confirmed to concern the same individual, this history is relevant to assessing his public record, although it does not, by itself, establish that his present allegations are false. Nevertheless, anyone who assumes the responsibility of publicly questioning another person’s integrity must be willing to demonstrate accuracy, transparency and fairness in their own conduct. Public influence is not proof of credibility. Credibility must be earned through consistency, evidence and accountability. THE ODIBOLA LAND CONTROVERSY: WHAT HAS BEEN LEFT OUT? The allegation attributed to Mezie suggests that Odibola Properties acquired disputed family land through Fabulous Amaewhule without the involvement of the wider family. Odibola Properties has challenged that account. According to the company’s explanation, it did not purchase the land directly from Fabulous Amaewhule. Rather, it became involved through a Power of Attorney granted by an association of medical doctors following an out-of-court settlement with Fabulous Amaewhule, whom the company identifies as a judgment creditor in earlier proceedings involving the doctors. This distinction is fundamental. A company acting under a Power of Attorney granted following a legal settlement is not necessarily in the same position as a developer accused of forcibly taking possession of another person’s land. Of course, the existence of a Power of Attorney does not automatically establish valid ownership or resolve competing claims. Its legal effect depends on the underlying rights, documents and court decisions. But if the allegation against Odibola was presented without properly examining these matters, the public is entitled to question whether the accusation was based on a complete investigation. WHY ODIBOLA’S RESPONSE DESERVES PUBLIC ATTENTION Rather than allowing allegations to define its reputation, Odibola Properties has continued to publicly explain its position and insist that its transactions should be assessed through verifiable documentation. This is an important standard for the real estate industry. A developer’s reputation should be judged by the legitimacy of its acquisitions, compliance with the law, fulfilment of contractual obligations and treatment of investors. Odibola’s willingness to present its account and refer to legal documentation offers the public an opportunity to examine the dispute beyond social media narratives. The company has also maintained that its commitment to real estate development and the protection of investors remains unchanged. These claims deserve fair and independent verification, just as the allegations against the company do. THE QUESTIONS MEZIE SHOULD ANSWER Before the public accepts any sweeping allegation of land grabbing, several questions deserve answers: 1. Did Mezie examine the relevant court judgments and settlement agreements before making his allegations? 2. Did he investigate the Power of Attorney under which Odibola says it operates? 3. Did he distinguish between a disputed land title and an allegation of unlawful or forcible land grabbing? 4. Did he give adequate consideration to the company’s explanation and supporting documents? 5. Is he willing to correct any material claim that the documentary evidence proves inaccurate? These are not personal attacks. They are reasonable standards of accountability for anyone seeking to influence public opinion. CONCLUSION: INTEGRITY IS ESTABLISHED BY EVIDENCE, NOT SOCIAL MEDIA NOISE The public must be careful not to confuse confidence on social media with competence in legal and property matters. A person’s ability to attract attention does not automatically qualify that person to determine ownership, interpret judgments or pronounce guilt in complex land disputes. Odibola Properties has built its public position around integrity, lawful acquisition and investor protection. Those commitments should be measured against its documents, transactions and actual performance, not merely against the volume of allegations directed at it. Equally, anyone making accusations against the company must be prepared to substantiate them with reliable evidence. Before believing allegations against Odibola Properties, ask to see the judgments, settlement documents, Power of Attorney and relevant title records. Before trusting any public commentator, examine the accuracy of their claims and their willingness to be held accountable. The future of real estate investment in Rivers State must be protected through due diligence, responsible advocacy and respect for the rule of law. ODIBOLA PROPERTIES LIMITED — BUILT ON INTEGRITY. She identified automation as another critical factor, noting that businesses must establish systems to ensure customers receive the services they have been promised. “We have to verify and ensure that things we promised our customers are what they get. item.title: ‘We’ll exhume him’ — Toluwanisings’ family rejects cemetery burial
item.description: The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Toluwanisings has threatened to exhume his remains if he is buried in a cemetery rather than beside his late mother at their ancestral home in Oyo State. A representative of the family, in a video circulating on social media, said relatives had agreed that the singer should be brought home and buried at their father’s compound, insisting that they would not accept any alternative arrangement. “We have all decided in the family that Toluwanisings must not be buried in the cemetery. For this reason, they should bring him back home,” the representative said. He warned that the family would take matters into its own hands if the singer were buried in a cemetery. “If you people decide to bury him in the cemetery, we will remove him from there. I am speaking on behalf of all the family members,” he added. The family representative also dismissed concerns about burying the singer at the house he built, insisting that their preferred location was beside his mother’s grave at their father’s compound in Oyo State. “If you say you can’t bury him in his house that he built, we don’t know your reasons and we don’t even care to know, just bring him home,” he said. The dispute has sparked reactions on social media, with some users arguing that the family should have a say in determining the singer’s final resting place. Others have called for a peaceful resolution that respects the deceased and his relatives. Toluwanisings, whose real name was Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, died on October 14, 2026, at the age of 41. He, however, noted that there was still time before the elections for the commission to address the concerns. “I therefore join other concerned Nigerians in calling on INEC to provide a clear explanation, establish the facts and take all necessary measures to clean up the register,” he said. Dickson urged Nigerians to take advantage of the statutory display of the voter register at designated locations to scrutinise entries and report suspicious or inaccurate information through appropriate channels. He also encouraged citizens to use INEC’s online platforms, where available, to verify relevant information and raise concerns about questionable entries. According to him, residents familiar with their communities and polling units could help identify suspicious registrations by reporting questionable names and photographs to the appropriate authorities for verification. “INEC must take responsibility for ensuring that the register is credible, accurate and reliable. The integrity of the voter register is fundamental to the integrity of the election, and the commission must do everything within its legal powers to protect it,” he said. Dickson urges vigilance over Ebola concerns Asked whether reported Ebola cases could lead to the postponement of the 2027 elections, Dickson urged Nigerians to remain vigilant, saying it was too early to determine the possible implications. He said Nigerians were awaiting further information from the Federal Government and relevant health authorities on the situation and measures being taken to contain the disease. “Whether the situation will affect the election is not something any of us can determine at this stage. We are waiting for more information, and all Nigerians must remain vigilant,” he said. Dickson said the government’s response should address broader public health concerns and contingency measures in the event of a worsening situation, rather than focus solely on possible effects on the elections. He added that information available to him suggested that the affected patient had been contained and the situation was being managed, but cautioned against making claims not supported by verified information. “We must all remain alert and prayerful. I urge Nigerians to exercise caution and call on governments at all levels to strengthen their preparedness and response mechanisms,” he said. He also urged Nigerians to avoid spreading unverified information or making unfounded predictions about the possible consequences of the outbreak. NDC calls for issue-based campaigns On the 2027 general elections, Dickson urged political parties and their supporters to focus on issues rather than resort to insults, abuse or violence. He said the NDC would promote an electoral process in which every eligible Nigerian’s vote counted. “The election must be ‘one person, one vote; one youth, one vote;’ and every Nigerian’s vote must count. As you return to your respective constituencies, I encourage you to take this message to the people and mobilise support for our candidates,” he said. He urged party members to explain their policies, engage citizens respectfully and persuade voters through issue-based campaigns. “Our party does not stand for violence or personal attacks. We want the ruling party to justify its claim to another term in office through its record of performance,” he said. Dickson described elections as a referendum on the performance of an incumbent government, expressing confidence that Nigerians would assess the record of the current administration before deciding how to vote. Group cites leadership deficit Earlier, Emmanuel said the Dickson Movement for Democracy was established in response to what it described as a leadership deficit in Nigeria and the need to groom a new generation of leaders committed to accountability, transparency and responsible governance. He said the group had identified Dickson as a potential mentor after assessing the country’s political landscape and seeking a role model whose leadership experience and philosophy could guide young Nigerians. Emmanuel said the movement was committed to preserving multiparty democracy and defending the country’s constitutional order. He expressed concern about what he described as a drift towards a one-party state, citing the movement of politicians towards the ruling party. According to him, the emergence of the NDC under Dickson’s leadership offered an alternative political direction and reinforced the need to preserve multiparty democracy. Emmanuel said the movement’s vision extended beyond the 2027 elections to developing future leaders and political ideologues committed to democratic governance and national development. He added that the group wanted an electoral process in which no vote was stolen, suppressed or unlawfully excluded from the final results. item.title: Osun IPAC disowns members on Adeleke’s PCC list
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) in Osun State has disowned individuals listed as representatives of political parties in the Osun Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) by Governor Ademola Adeleke, the state coordinator of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council. In a statement issued on Tuesday and endorsed by 11 political parties, Osun IPAC said the individuals listed as its representatives were acting on their own and had not been authorised to represent the council. The parties include Action Alliance, National Rescue Movement, Action Democratic Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party and National Democratic Party. Others are Democratic Leadership Alliance, African Action Congress, Labour Party, Zenith Labour Party and All Progressives Grand Alliance. An advertorial signed by Adeleke and published in a national newspaper had listed Odeleye Titus, Faribido Benson, Enorch Olalekan, Adetunji Olubunmi, Prince Adesoji Adeleke and Rev. Olatunji Popoola as IPAC representatives in the Osun PCC. However, the council said the inclusion of their names was misleading and could create confusion over its representation. “We wish to state categorically and for the record, that the persons whose names were paraded as IPAC members in the said council are not our representatives, nor were they, at any point in time, nominated or authorised by the council to represent us in any capacity,” the statement said. IPAC described itself as a structured body with recognised leadership and member political parties, insisting that any representation must follow due process and official communication from its secretariat. The council said it completely dissociated itself from the list, warning against using its name to score political points or create a false impression of broad-based acceptance. It also urged President Tinubu not to recognise the individuals listed as its representatives in the Osun PCC, insisting that its legitimate stakeholders were parties with strong grassroots presence across the state’s local government areas. “We are the majority members of IPAC in Osun State with strong grassroots presence across all local governments, and any engagement with IPAC in the state should be through us,” the statement added. item.title: Oborevwori signs five bills into law in Delta
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi and Ochuko Akuopha ASABA — Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has signed five bills into law, saying the measures are aimed at strengthening public institutions, improving service delivery and securing a better future for residents. Oborevwori assented to the bills at Government House, Asaba, on Wednesday, describing them as part of his administration’s reform efforts under the MORE Agenda. “I assented to five bills, three amendments, one consolidated, and a brand-new one passed by the Delta State House of Assembly,” the governor said. The new laws are the Delta State Revenue Service (Consolidated) Law, 2026; Delta State Public and Private Properties Protection (Amendment) Law, 2026; High Court (Amendment) Law, 2026; Customary Court of Appeal (Amendment) Law, 2026; and Payment of Thirteenth Month Salary Law, 2026. Oborevwori said the laws would strengthen accountability, protect public assets, reinforce the rule of law and improve workers’ morale. “Together, we have strengthened accountability, safeguarded public assets, reinforced the rule of law and boosted public servants’ morale,” he said. He added that the measures reflected his administration’s determination to build institutions that serve residents with fairness, efficiency and respect. “These efforts reflect our resolve to build institutions that serve our people with fairness, efficiency and respect, while securing a better future for our people,” he said. The governor stressed that development went beyond infrastructure to include policies capable of improving people’s lives. On the Thirteenth Month Salary Law, Oborevwori said the initiative was intended to boost workers’ morale, reward their contributions and improve productivity. He also said the amendments to the laws governing the judiciary would increase the number of High Court judges from 46 to 50 and Customary Court of Appeal judges from nine to 12, with a view to improving justice delivery. According to him, the laws would strengthen public institutions, improve service delivery and promote economic development. Presenting the bills, Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Emomotimi Guwor, said the measures would strengthen governance, improve justice delivery and protect investments. One train on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha was seen embedded into another after the second such accident to strike Spain this year. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Civil Guard on October 28, 2026 shows an aerial scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. (Photo by Handout / Guardia Civil / AFP) Some carriages were lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment, while dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site. “We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more,” Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31. A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha government said that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition. Helicopters hovered above the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour.
